titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 61: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 61. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲝⲁ] (top right) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes); the running title [ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ] is restored in brackets, with a stroke over the restored ⲙ. Line 1 is a row of 29 illegible dots (556–1298, one of area 2 at 609) at the zone centre; `bands` does not list it and its y comes from `dots`. Every dot run on the page was counted from the `dots` x-positions between the bracket positions and checked on the 4× halves. Reconcile flags explained: l. 1 the dot at 609 has area 2; ll. 3, 5 (722, 748, 921, 948), 7, 22 (the four bracket dots) and 25 (the three opening dots) have dots at the zone centre (y ≤ centre + 1), which reconcile does not count; ll. 2 and 12 count a piece of the margin numeral (470); l. 15 counts the point of the printed "(?)" (1182/907); l. 16 counts a fragment of "leer" (912/946); l. 31 misses the first dot (565), which touches the bracket.
